entries.name: DEFAULT_FETCH_ABORT_ERROR_NAMES
entries.description:
The `.name` / class names that mean "the client gave up waiting": the DOMException `AbortError` / `TimeoutError` an
`AbortSignal` rejects with, and util/fetch's own `FetchTimeoutError`.

entries.name: DEFAULT_FETCH_NETWORK_ERROR_CODES
entries.description:
The Node / undici socket codes a `fetch` failure carries (on the error or its `cause`) when the far end never
answered: refused, reset, unreachable or timed out.

A DNS miss (`ENOTFOUND`) is left out: a misspelled host is a fact a resend cannot change. Add it to a custom set to
treat it as transient.

entries.name: DEFAULT_FETCH_NETWORK_ERROR_MESSAGES
entries.description:
The `TypeError` messages a `fetch` rejects with when the request never got an answer, by runtime:

| Message | Source |
|---|---|
| `fetch failed` | Node / undici |
| `Failed to fetch` | Chromium |
| `NetworkError when attempting to fetch resource.` | Firefox |
| `Load failed` | Safari 17+ |
| `The Internet connection appears to be offline.` | Safari 16 |

CAVEAT: a browser reports a CORS rejection, mixed content or an extension block with the same `Failed to fetch`,
and nothing tells them apart by design. Such an error reads as transient; the caller's bounded attempt budget caps
the cost.

entries.name: DEFAULT_FETCH_TRANSIENT_HTTP_STATUSES
entries.description:
The HTTP statuses below 500 that are transient: 408 (Request Timeout — the request was never processed, so a resend
is safe) and 429 (Too Many Requests). Every status `>= 500` is transient as well.

entries.name: DEFAULT_FETCH_PERMANENT_HTTP_STATUSES
entries.description:
The HTTP statuses that are permanent: 400, 401, 402, 403 and 404 — facts about the request or the credential that a
resend cannot change.

entries.name: readFetchErrorStatus
entries.description:
Reads the HTTP status off a thrown value: its own numeric `status`, else its `response.status` (util/fetch's
`FetchResponseError` and the `{ response }` shape a limited fetch throws).

params.name: error
params.description: - The thrown value.

entries.returns: The status, or `undefined` when neither is a number.
entries.example:
readFetchErrorStatus({ status: 429 }); // 429
readFetchErrorStatus(new FetchResponseError(new Response(null, { status: 503 }))); // 503
readFetchErrorStatus(new Error('boom')); // undefined

entries.name: classifyFetchErrorStatus
entries.description:
Classifies an HTTP status, in order: a `permanentStatuses` status is `permanent`; a `transientStatuses` status or
any status `>= 500` is `transient`; anything else (409, 405, 410, 422, a 2xx with a bad body, a 3xx) is `unknown`.

params.name: status
params.description: - The HTTP status.

params.name: config
params.description: - Optional replacement status sets.

entries.name: isFetchAbortError
entries.description:
Whether a thrown value is an ABORT / timeout error: its `.name`, or a constructor name on its chain, is in
`abortErrorNames` (the DOMException `AbortError` / `TimeoutError`, util/fetch's `FetchTimeoutError`, plus any
SDK class a caller adds).

{@link classifyFetchError} reads an abort as `transient`, because a timer that fired is worth a resend. A caller that
cancelled on purpose checks its own signal before resending.

params.name: error
params.description: - The thrown value.

params.name: config
params.description: - Optional replacement name set.

entries.name: isFetchNetworkError
entries.description:
Whether a thrown value is a NETWORK failure — the request never got an answer.

The checks run in this order.

1. Gather the string `code` of the error and of its direct `cause`.
2. Any gathered code in `networkErrorCodes` → a network failure.
3. Codes exist but none is in the set → NOT a network failure. A specific code outranks the generic message, so
   undici's `TypeError('fetch failed')` with a `cause.code` of `ENOTFOUND` or a TLS / certificate code is not one.
4. No code at all: the error OR its direct cause is a `TypeError` whose message is in `networkErrorMessages`
   (Node's `fetch failed` and the browser messages in {@link DEFAULT_FETCH_NETWORK_ERROR_MESSAGES}). The cause level
   catches a wrapper that keeps the native failure as its cause.

params.name: error
params.description: - The thrown value.

params.name: config
params.description: - Optional replacement code and message sets.

entries.example:
isFetchNetworkError(new TypeError('fetch failed', { cause: { code: 'ECONNREFUSED' } })); // true
isFetchNetworkError(new TypeError('Failed to fetch')); // true (Chromium)
isFetchNetworkError(new TypeError('fetch failed', { cause: { code: 'ENOTFOUND' } })); // false

entries.name: classifyFetchError

params.name: error
params.description: - The thrown value.

params.name: config
params.description: - Optional sets and status reader.

entries.example:
classifyFetchError({ status: 503 }); // 'transient'
classifyFetchError(new TypeError('Failed to fetch')); // 'transient'
classifyFetchError({ status: 401 }); // 'permanent'
classifyFetchError(new Error('boom')); // 'unknown'

entries.name: isRetryableFetchErrorClassification
entries.description:
The shared resend rule: `transient` → `true`, `permanent` → `false`, `unknown` →
`isRetryableUnknownError(error) ?? retryUnknownByDefault`. The function is never consulted for a `transient` or
`permanent` error.

params.name: config
params.description: - The classification, the error, the host function and the caller's default.

entries.example:
isRetryableFetchErrorClassification({ classification: 'unknown', error, retryUnknownByDefault: false }); // false
isRetryableFetchErrorClassification({ classification: 'unknown', error, isRetryableUnknownError: () => true, retryUnknownByDefault: false }); // true

entries.name: toBracketNotationSearchParamTuples
entries.description:
Expands a potentially nested object into bracket-notation query key/value tuples.

Arrays are addressed by index and object properties by key, recursively, so every leaf
gets its own fully-qualified parameter. Nullish leaves are omitted rather than emitted
as the strings `"null"`/`"undefined"`; all other leaves are stringified.

params.name: input
params.description: - The object to expand.

entries.name: makeUrlSearchParams
entries.signature: makeUrlSearchParams(input: Maybe<ArrayOrValue<Maybe<object | Record<string, string | number>>>>, options?: Maybe<MakeUrlSearchParamsOptions>): URLSearchParams
entries.description: Creates URLSearchParams from the input objects. The input objects are merged together.

params.name: input
params.description: - One or more objects (or nullish values) whose key-value pairs become search parameters.

params.name: options
params.description: - Optional configuration for filtering, omitting keys, and space encoding.

entries.returns: A URLSearchParams instance built from the merged and filtered input.

entries.name: makeUrlSearchParamsString
entries.signature: makeUrlSearchParamsString(input: Maybe<ArrayOrValue<Maybe<object | Record<string, string | number>>>>, options?: Maybe<MakeUrlSearchParamsOptions>): string
entries.description:
Creates a URL query string from the input objects.

Equivalent to `makeUrlSearchParams(...).toString()`, but respects the
{@link MakeUrlSearchParamsOptions.useUrlSearchSpaceHandling} option to produce
RFC 3986 percent-encoded output (`%20` for spaces) instead of the
`application/x-www-form-urlencoded` default (`+` for spaces).

params.name: input
params.description: - Objects to encode as query parameters.

params.name: options
params.description: - Encoding options.

entries.returns: The encoded query string (without a leading `?`)

entries.name: updateUrlSearchParams
entries.signature: updateUrlSearchParams(url: string, params: Maybe<ArrayOrValue<Maybe<object | Record<string, string | number>>>>, options?: Maybe<MakeUrlSearchParamsOptions>): string
entries.description:
Updates or adds query parameters on an existing URL string.

Parses the URL's existing query string, merges in the new parameters (new values
override existing keys), and returns the rebuilt URL. Respects all
{@link MakeUrlSearchParamsOptions} such as `omitKeys`, `filterEmptyValues`, and
`useUrlSearchSpaceHandling`.

params.name: url
params.description: - The URL string to update.

params.name: params
params.description: - New search parameters to merge into the URL.

params.name: options
params.description: - Optional configuration for filtering, omitting keys, and space encoding.

entries.returns: The URL string with updated query parameters.

entries.name: mergeMakeUrlSearchParamsOptions
entries.description: Merges an array of MakeUrlSearchParamsOptions into a single MakeUrlSearchParamsOptions value.

params.name: options
params.description: - One or more options objects whose omitKeys sets are combined.

entries.returns: A single MakeUrlSearchParamsOptions with the union of all omitKeys.

entries.name: readFetchJsonText
entries.description:
Awaits a fetch, reads its body as text once, and decodes that text as JSON.

Never throws for a non-ok status or a non-JSON body: the caller reads `response.ok`, `parsed` and `text`. Rejects only
when the request itself or the body read fails, with that original error, so a later classifier still sees it.

params.name: responsePromise
params.description: - The pending fetch. A caller already holding a Response passes `Promise.resolve(response)`.

params.name: config
params.description: - Optional decoder override.

entries.returns: The response, its raw text and the decoded value.

entries.name: fetchJsonTextDecodeResponseFunction
entries.description:
Creates a {@link FetchJsonDecodeResponseFunction} built on {@link readFetchJsonText}.

Rejects with a {@link JsonResponseParseError} when the text is not JSON, so the configured parse-error handler still runs.
The decoder consumes the body, so the handler cannot re-read it; `response.json()` behaves the same way.

params.name: config
params.description: - Optional decoder override, e.g. a repairing `parseJson`.

entries.returns: A decoder to pass as {@link FetchJsonFunctionConfig.decodeResponse}.

entries.name: parseRetryAfterHeader
entries.description: Parses an HTTP `Retry-After` header: either delay-seconds (`120`) or an HTTP-date (`Wed, 21 Oct 2026 07:28:00 GMT`).

params.name: value
params.description: - The header value.

params.name: now
params.description: - The current time, for an HTTP-date. Defaults to now.

entries.returns: The milliseconds to wait (0 for a date in the past), or undefined when the header is absent or unparseable.

entries.name: readFetchErrorRetryAfter
entries.description:
Reads a server-requested retry wait off a thrown error — `error.headers`, else `error.response.headers` (a `Headers`
or anything with `get(name)`, or a plain record read case-insensitively). The non-standard `retry-after-ms` (OpenAI,
Azure) wins when it reads as a finite number ≥ 0; else `Retry-After` through {@link parseRetryAfterHeader}.

Browser-safe: no Node import.

params.name: error
params.description: - The thrown value — an SDK error with `headers`, a `FetchResponseError`, anything else.

params.name: now
params.description: - The current time, for an HTTP-date `Retry-After`. Defaults to now.

entries.returns: The milliseconds to wait, or undefined when the error carries no readable wait.
entries.example:
readFetchErrorRetryAfter({ headers: new Headers({ 'retry-after': '2' }) }); // 2000
readFetchErrorRetryAfter({ headers: { 'Retry-After': '1', 'retry-after-ms': '1500' } }); // 1500
readFetchErrorRetryAfter(new Error('boom')); // undefined
